issue.title: Null pointer dereference in `array_repeat` via re-entrant `__index__` during array multiplication

labels.name: extension-modules
labels.description: C modules in the Modules dir

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

issue.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This issue is not for newcomers.

### What happened?

A custom `__index__` can swap the MRO of an `array.array` subclass mid multiplication, so `array_repeat` calls `find_array_state_by_type` on a type without the array module and receives a NULL module state. The subsequent dereference of `state->ArrayType` then hits freed memory and triggers a null pointer read.

**Proof of Concept:**
```python
import array

class Good(array.array):
    pass

class Hide(type):
    def mro(cls):
        return (cls, object)

class Bad(Good, metaclass=Hide):
    pass

arr = Good('b', b'x')

class Count:
    def __index__(self):
        arr.__class__ = Bad     # Drop array.array from the MRO mid-op
        return 2

arr * Count()
```

**Related Code Snippet**

<details>

```
#define find_array_state_by_type(tp) \
      (get_array_state(PyType_GetModuleByDef(tp, &arraymodule)))   // requires array.array in the MRO

static array_state *
get_array_state(PyObject *module)
{
    return (array_state *)_PyModule_GetState(module);            // assumes module is non-NULL
}

static PyObject *
array_repeat(PyObject *op, Py_ssize_t n)
{
    arrayobject *a = arrayobject_CAST(op);
    array_state *state = find_array_state_by_type(Py_TYPE(a));

    if (n < 0)
        n = 0;
    const Py_ssize_t array_length = Py_SIZE(a);
    if ((array_length != 0) && (n > PY_SSIZE_T_MAX / array_length)) {
        return PyErr_NoMemory();
    }
    Py_ssize_t size = array_length * n;
    arrayobject* np = (arrayobject *) newarrayobject(state->ArrayType, size, a->ob_descr);
    if (np == NULL)
        return NULL;
    if (size == 0)
        return (PyObject *)np;

    const Py_ssize_t oldbytes = array_length * a->ob_descr->itemsize;
    const Py_ssize_t newbytes = oldbytes * n;
    _PyBytes_Repeat(np->ob_item, newbytes, a->ob_item, oldbytes);

    return (PyObject *)np;
}
```

</details>

comments.body:
This may be a broader issue where the module's state of heap types is incorrectly accessed. The current design requires extension modules to have multiple calls (first get the module from the type via one of the available functions and then get its state). 

I think we need to address this by first gathering the heap types that are affected by this pattern and then possibly add an internal function for safely fetching their state from the module definition. For non-subclassable heap types, we could skip some checks though (and really want a crash because some assertion would be failing).

> [!IMPORTANT] 
> As such, this issue is **NOT** for newcomers.
